title: Delete stops dropping a piece once you have undone a delete
goal: Cut a recording into three pieces, pick the middle one and press Delete: it goes. Press undo and it comes back. Press Delete again and nothing happens, because the key is no longer reaching the command that drops a piece. A person cutting a recording tries a delete, changes their mind, changes it back, and the key has quietly stopped answering.
notes:
REPRODUCED 2026-09-22 by the digest pass, on the probe built from 5ac6ce15, twice (once inside the full sweep, once on its own).

  Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/delete-key-drops-a-piece-walk.json --no-build
  -> step 23 (shortcut): delete should have gone to Video ▸ Delete This Piece but was taken by window

The walk gets that far cleanly: three pieces, the middle one deleted (step 17 passes, stage 2-delete-dropped-the-middle-piece), then action videoUndoEdit, then expectRecording pieces 3 keeps 3 seconds 8 passes, so the undo itself is right and the document really is back to three pieces. It is only the SECOND Delete that misses. So the piece is coming back without whatever makes Delete This Piece the key's owner: either the piece selection is not restored by the undo, or the menu item is left disabled.

Found in the 2026-09-22T12:10Z full sweep (queue/sweep/2026-09-22-031225.log), which named 16 failing walks; this is the only one of them in the focus epic, which is why it is out on its own rather than left in walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep-4.
acceptance: After a delete and an undo, pressing Delete on the piece that came back drops it again, in one press
The Video menu's Delete This Piece is the thing the key reaches, not whatever the window does with a bare Delete
delete-key-drops-a-piece-walk passes twice on its own
One undo puts the piece back each time, however many times the pair is repeated

log.note: Same shape as a-shape-that-was-turned-into-a-picture-and-undon, which is being dropped today because its own walk (turn-two-shapes-into-pictures-walk) now passes and image-editing is staged later: there, a marquee plus Backspace went silent after two undos; here, Delete goes silent after one. Two surfaces, one pattern: an undo puts the document back without putting back whatever made the delete key belong to that command. Worth checking for a third case while this one is open.
